title: Chiral Color Ice: Exact Local Handedness Constraints and Möbius Zero Modes in Frustrated Magnets
authors: Péter Kránitz, Yasir Iqbal, Karlo Penc
abstract: Local constraints govern the low-energy physics of frustrated matter, but familiar ice-type rules constrain flux-like quantities and are insensitive to handedness. Here we show that handedness itself can be imposed as an exact local quantum constraint without selecting an axis in spin space. We construct positive-semidefinite, SU(2)-invariant parent Hamiltonians whose complete zero-energy space on a tetrahedron has a prescribed chirality sign, rather than selecting a particular chiral wave function. For spin-1/2 the local term is a rank-one projector onto a chiral tetrahedral singlet, while for arbitrary spin it factorizes as $B^\dagger B$ through a singlet-annihilation operator, with a completely characterized kernel given by the span of the globally rotated chiral color-ice states. For coherent states, the same zero-energy condition becomes an $S$-independent nonlinear constraint in which three spin directions determine the fourth through a Möbius transformation; compositions of these maps define constraint holonomies on extended lattices. Connecting the same local constraint in different ways produces qualitatively different collective regimes: corner-sharing lattices retain exponentially large quantum ground-state kernels, with rigorous lower bounds exceeding conventional ice benchmarks; edge-sharing lattices support subdimensional plane or line zero modes; while triangular constructions suppress nonuniform coherent deformations and contain the complete Anderson tower of tetrahedral magnetic order at exactly zero energy. Two inequivalent triangular coverings further show that harmonic zero-mode counting does not determine the size of the quantum kernel. These results establish a tractable setting in which local handedness, nonlinear constraint geometry, and quantum degeneracy can be disentangled and related directly to the connectivity of the constraint network.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to impose exact, local chirality constraints on frustrated magnetic systems, moving beyond achiral ice rules. By constructing specific Hamiltonians, the authors show that the resulting quantum ground-state degeneracy is highly sensitive to the underlying lattice connectivity. This provides a rigorous method to study chiral quantum magnetism in correlated materials.
main_problem: To construct a local, positive-semidefinite, SU(2)-invariant quantum Hamiltonian that enforces an exact local constraint corresponding to a specific handedness (chirality) in frustrated magnets without selecting a specific spin-space axis.
main_result: The local constraint can be enforced exactly, leading to ground-state kernels whose degeneracy depends critically on the lattice connectivity (corner-sharing vs. triangular).
method: The authors construct parent Hamiltonians using singlet-annihilation operators and analyze the resulting zero-energy subspace, particularly in the coherent state limit governed by Möbius transformations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Chiral Color Ice (CCI) constraints in frustrated magnets, generalizing standard ice rules to incorporate time-reversal symmetry breaking (chirality) on tetrahedral units.
key_observables: Quantum ground-state kernel size/degeneracy, the presence of subdimensional zero modes, and the specific chirality sign of the zero-energy space.
important_parameters: Spin quantum number (S), lattice geometry (corner-sharing, edge-sharing, triangular), and the degree of frustration.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing parent Hamiltonians that project onto the chiral subspace, and in the coherent limit, the constraint is described by a Möbius transformation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the elementary motif of chiral color ice on a tetrahedron, confirming the structure possesses a definite handedness via scalar chirality.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the chiral local constraint on a tetrahedron to analyzing its realization via parent Hamiltonians for arbitrary spin. It then examines the resulting zero-energy physics on different lattice topologies (corner-sharing, edge-sharing, triangular) and concludes by analyzing the symmetry content using group theory.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between local geometric constraints (chirality) and the resulting quantum degeneracy provides a powerful, tunable framework for modeling exotic quantum phases in strongly correlated materials.
